title: Commerce Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit the composed commerce contract without merging capability ownership.
owner: Storefront, Store, Product, Pricing, Inventory, Units, workflow, publishing, cache, and search owners
summary: Commerce integration passes stable identities and verified context between modules; no module writes another capability's models directly.

sections.heading: Capability ownership
items: Storefront owns hostname and website context, Store owns commercial touchpoints, Product owns identity and catalog data, Pricing owns monetary resolution, and Inventory owns stock.
Units owns reusable measurement semantics, CMS owns presentation content, Workflow owns approval, and nPublish owns staged-to-Online orchestration.
Composition happens through authenticated contracts; BackOffice and Storefront do not proxy every business operation or duplicate authoritative records.

sections.heading: Context and resolution
items: Trusted context can include tenant, enterprise, site, Store, country, region, channel, locale, currency, customer, segment, catalog, and effective time.
A hostname narrows context through Storefront configuration. Browser values cannot broaden tenant, select another site's catalog, or claim customer-specific price eligibility.
Pricing and Inventory independently validate the context dimensions relevant to their decisions and return provenance-safe explanations.

sections.heading: Authoring and delivery
items: Business users author versioned capabilities in staged catalogs where configured, associate exact changed items with workflows, and publish approved versions to separate Online targets.
Online services use database authority with bounded cache and search projections for traffic. Invalidation and indexing follow successful authoritative persistence.
Different sites under one enterprise can use separate content and product catalogs, Stores, prices, and warehouse sourcing while sharing selected capabilities deliberately.

sections.heading: Consistency and failure
items: A product may exist without price or stock; missing optional content may degrade, while ambiguous price or uncertain stock commitment follows explicit failure policy.
Reservations, allocations, movements, transfers, and reconciliation use concurrency and idempotency. Prices use deterministic eligibility, priority, specificity, currency, unit, and date.
Derived cache or search outage never silently changes authoritative Product, Price, or Stock data and must be recoverable by rebuild or reconciliation.

sections.heading: Verification checklist
items: Test multi-site, multi-store, multi-country, multi-zone, customer segment, unit, quantity tier, effective date, staged/Online, and cross-tenant scenarios.
Test context spoofing, missing and ambiguous data, duplicate commands, concurrent orders, provider outages, partial publishing, cache/search recovery, reconciliation, and rollback.
Measure customer latency, price and stock resolution, reservation contention, publication and projection lag, dependency health, and business correctness under load.

sections.heading: Contract checklist
items: Tenant, enterprise, Site, Store, country, channel, locale, currency, catalog, customer/segment, product/variant, unit, and time context.
Stable cross-module references and audience-bound Storefront handle.
Independent authorization, validation, persistence, cache, search, version, workflow, and publishing authority.
Staged/Online topology, target transport, derived refresh, audit, reconciliation, rollback, and compensation.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, cross-tenant, performance, failure, security, and regression tests.
